ground_truth.title: State v. Marcus Reed
ground_truth.location: St. Agnes Catholic Church, Cedar Grove

defendant.name: Marcus Reed
defendant.background: Former network engineer, responsible for church’s digital security

victim.name: St. Agnes Church
victim.description: Historic Catholic parish with a 12th‑century crucifix and a 15th‑century fresco

ground_truth.what_really_happened: On the night of March 14, Marcus Reed used his knowledge of the church’s security system to disable the motion sensors covering the main altar. He entered the sanctuary during a midnight Mass and removed the fresco panel, placing it in a storage locker. He then restored the sensors and left unnoticed. The fresco was discovered missing the next morning by the parish secretary. No other persons had access to the altar area that night.

timeline.event: Reed logs into church network from the IT office
Reed disables motion sensors on altar wall
Reed enters sanctuary during midnight Mass
Reed removes fresco panel and stores it in a locked locker
Reed restores motion sensors, exits church

evidence.name: Security Camera Footage
evidence.description: Video from the altar camera shows a figure moving toward the fresco at 23:20.
evidence.truth_note: The footage is a true recording of the suspect’s approach; the suspect is wearing a generic hoodie, not revealing identity.

evidence.name: Unlocked Motion Sensors Log
evidence.description: Digital log shows sensors disabled between 23:10 and 23:55.
evidence.truth_note: Reed is the only person with credentials to alter the sensors, making the log a factual record of his action.

evidence.name: Paint Residue on Gloves
evidence.description: Microscopic analysis finds pigment residues matching the fresco on a pair of gloves found near the altar.
evidence.truth_note: Gloves were found discarded by a volunteer; residue indicates contact with the fresco, consistent with the theft.

evidence.name: Parish Secretary's Testimony
evidence.description: Witness claimed to have seen a dark figure enter the altar after Mass.
evidence.truth_note: The secretary’s testimony is credible but the figure’s identity was unrecognized; she was biased in favor of the parish’s reputation.

evidence.name: Reed's Backup Storage Device
evidence.description: A USB drive found in the church’s server room contains photos of the fresco and the altar.
evidence.truth_note: The drive was placed there by a volunteer for archival purposes; Reed had no access to it at the time of the theft.

evidence.name: Fingerprint on the Lock
evidence.description: A partial fingerprint was recovered from the locker’s lock, matching a resident volunteer.
evidence.truth_note: The volunteer had access to the locker during the day; the print was left during a routine maintenance check.

witnesses.name: Ellen Carter
witnesses.knows: Saw a dark figure after Mass and heard muffled voices
witnesses.bias: Protecting the church’s reputation; wants to avoid scandal

witnesses.name: Thomas Nguyen
witnesses.knows: Was inside the church at 23:15 and saw lights turn off
witnesses.bias: Personal admiration for Reed; tends to speak positively about him
